_what_this_is: THE MEASUREMENT THE MUTATION RUNG'S CLOCK IS DERIVED FROM. harness/mutation_budget.py
computes budget = ceil(p100(total_seconds for a scope) * headroom / 60) * 60, and
scripts/factory_evidence_spine.py all read their timeout from that derivation instead of
carrying a literal. tests/factory/test_factory_mutation_budget.py pins the relation, so
the only way to raise a budget is to record the run that justifies it.
Two scopes, because two callers bound two different things: 'mutation-rung' is the whole
rung harness/ci.py runs (the application family and the factory family nested inside it),
'factory-family' is a standalone harness/factory_mutations/run.py (the nested call and the
kind='measured' is a wall clock somebody read off a real end-to-end run. kind='projected'
is composed from measured parts and says so, in `source`, with the parts. A projection is
a placeholder for the first real measurement, not a substitute for it: the runners print
MUTATIONS_SECONDS / FACTORY_MUTATIONS_SECONDS and per-defect MUTATION_TIMING lines, so the
first full run replaces these entries with observations.

measurements.environment: ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted runner, 4 vCPU (the validation host)
measurements.source: 2674s application family + 2962s factory family. Application: ten iterations (one clean baseline plus nine defects), each running all four channels; the quick channel is the whole cost and was measured at 179.027s, 203.383s and 207.4s on three ubuntu runs (worker runs 34066408781 rehead-quick-gate, 34061371205 quick-gate, and the quick-authority job of run 34066129225), p100 207.4s, plus a 60s allowance for holdout+citation+security (security --worktree measured at 0.39s locally and ~1.4s in CI; holdout and citation are bounded by the 84.3s that the ladder's app-start+e2e+holdout segment cost in run 34066724127). Factory: 391 defects, four concurrent copies, each copy's focused suite stopped at its first red file in the baseline's own cheapest-first order; the 72-file suite was measured file-by-file at 235.3s total on the maintainer's Windows host, whose measured cost distribution gives an expected 30.3s per caught defect (12.9% of the suite) => 391 * 30.3 / 4 = 2962s, taking no credit for the CI runner being faster than that host.
measurements.note: The 900s literal this replaces was never measured. Run 34066724127 (PR #134) passed security, provenance, all five judges, static, unit, the browser journey and the holdout, then died on 'TIMEOUT after 900s / GATE_FAILED: mutations' while still inside the application family - which alone projects to 2674s, 2.97x the budget it was given.

measurements.environment: maintainer Windows host (per-file measurement), four concurrent copies
measurements.source: 391 defects across the eight manifests, one copy each, four concurrent. Per-file wall clock of the whole 72-file focused suite measured on 2026-09-07 at origin/main 6a7f8c6: 235.3s total, median 0.59s, p90 7.81s, max 60.7s (test_factory_bootstrap.py). Stopping at the first red in cheapest-first order gives an expected 30.3s per caught defect against that distribution; 391 * 30.3 / 4 = 2962s.
measurements.note: Without the reduction the same catalogue is 391 * 235.3 / 4 = 23,000s (383 minutes) on that host. Before the reduction it could not run at all: TEST_FILES selected every copied path under tests/, including recorded JSON fixtures that run_tests executed as Python, three of which exit non-zero, so the family refused with 'focused baseline is red' whenever it was reached.

_raise_this: By recording the run that justifies it, in the same reviewed change. A budget raised without a measurement behind it is the literal this file exists to retire.
